YouTube refused plain downloads with HTTP 403; every picture download used --js-runtimes node --extractor-args youtube:player_client=android, and the long broadcasts were fetched as --download-sections windows. Times are seconds into the YouTube video. Nothing found for a 2025 or 2026 newsroom knocked off air by a hack while covering it; the 2024 CrowdStrike day is the only real footage of anchors apologising for their own station's computers.

candidates.name: 02-abc-au-unprecedented-computer-shutdown
candidates.event: CrowdStrike outage, 19 July 2024; ABC special edition in place of the 7pm news
candidates.speaker: anchor at desk
candidates.quote: companies and government agencies worldwide tonight in the grips of an unprecedented computer shutdown that's affecting banks, airports, telecommunications, supermarkets and small businesses
candidates.onScreenText: ABC NEWS bug bottom right only; no chyron (their graphics were down)
candidates.picture: Jeremy Fernandez standing at the ABC News desk, newsroom monitors behind him, no lower third
candidates.editPlan: For 8 s keep 9.9-17.0 ('companies and government agencies worldwide ... affecting banks, airports'). For 12 s keep 9.9-21.9. If longer is wanted, add 24.2-31.2 ('the impact is widespread, flights are grounded, payment systems are down and some health care services affected') but drop 19.96-24.2, which says 'it began about 3pm Eastern Standard Time'. The 7.7-9.9 'I'm Jeremy Fernandez' can be dropped or kept; the picture is the same shot throughout.
candidates.caveats: Says 'computer shutdown' rather than 'slow down and become unusable'; 2024 footage. Nothing in the window names CrowdStrike or Microsoft; the words 'not a cyber attack' do not occur in this opening.

candidates.onScreenText: GLOBAL TECH OUTAGE lower third with CBS NEWS NEW YORK bug; a small news ticker at the very bottom scrolls 'after a CrowdStrike update caused a global Microsoft outage' and a '4:58 PM' clock
candidates.picture: Windows 'Recovery' blue screen full frame, then newsroom monitors all blue, then airport queues; from 44 s Dick Brennan and Kristine Johnson at the desk under a GLOBAL TECH OUTAGE wall graphic

Longer: keep 2.0-9.3 plus 11.4-18.6 ('it crippled operations, everything from hospitals and banks to small businesses and airports'). Drop 1.08-2.0 ('and right now at 5'). candidates.name: 04-cbs-evening-cloud-digital-backbone
candidates.event: AWS us-east-1 outage, 20 October 2025; Kelly O'Grady package and desk chat
candidates.speaker: correspondent voice over graphics, then correspondent on camera at the anchor desk
candidates.quote: Amazon's cloud service called AWS went down across the country, causing websites and apps to stop working. The cloud is the digital backbone of the modern internet. AWS is a 100 billion dollar business that provides everything from data storage to security for millions of customers. For example, instead of building and maintaining their own physical servers, companies instead rent from AWS. Organizations large and small rely on the tech giant.
candidates.onScreenText: MASSIVE OUTAGE / Global Sites Down after Cloud Service Fails; CBS Evening News bug
candidates.picture: 19-47 s: AWS logo on a phone, 'AWS Services: Computing & Hosting, Storage & Backup, Databases & Security, Networking & Delivery' graphic, server racks, Downdetector logo wall, 'AWS Outage' warning graphic. 64-112 s: Kelly O'Grady on camera at the Evening News desk in a red dress with the two anchors, same chyron
candidates.editPlan: 15 s splice: 23.7-28.4 ('The cloud is the digital backbone of the modern internet', VO over the AWS graphic) + 92.2-101.8 (on camera at the desk: 'Companies rely on the cloud. I think the takeaway here is when you have so few major cloud companies, even just when one glitches, it causes a ripple effect'). Alternative: 19.4-28.4 + 41.7-47.2 ('Organizations large and small rely on the tech giant') for a 15 s all-VO version. candidates.name: 04-sky-aws-underpins-millions-of-companies
candidates.event: AWS us-east-1 outage, 20 October 2025; Sky News recap with correspondent Amelia Harper
candidates.speaker: correspondent voice over B-roll and explainer graphics; on camera in the newsroom at 3-25 s
candidates.quote: Now, this is a little bit complicated, but we'll keep it quite simple. So the cause has been identified as retail giant Amazon's cloud computing service called Amazon Web Services, and AWS, it provides on-demand cloud computing services over the internet, and what this really means, so that you know we can understand it, companies rent IT resources like servers or storage or databases instead of buying and maintaining their own physical hardware, and this AWS infrastructure underpins millions of companies' websites and platforms. So millions of businesses are going to be affected when there is an issue with this AWS system.
candidates.onScreenText: BREAKING NEWS / AWS: Seeing significant signs of recovery after outage (yellow Sky breaking strap); at 0-5 s 'Major internet outage affects dozens of websites'; 'Sky Correspondent Amelia Harper' name bar at about 5 s
candidates.picture: 77-105 s server-room cable B-roll; 105-120 s an AWS 'What Is Cloud Computing?' / 'What Is Amazon Web Services?' diagram credited 'Pictures: Amazon Web Services'; 3-25 s Amelia Harper standing in the Sky newsroom talking to camera
candidates.editPlan: 15 s: keep 106.7-119.5 ('and this AWS infrastructure underpins millions of companies' websites and platforms. So millions of businesses are going to be affected when there is an issue with this AWS system'), optionally preceded by 86.5-95.0 ('AWS, it provides on-demand cloud computing services over the internet, and what this really means, so that we can understand it'). If an on-camera presenter is wanted, lay the sound over her stand-up at 6.0-20.0; otherwise the explainer graphic plays as a newsroom insert.
candidates.caveats: The picture under the key line is a diagram, not a desk; the strap says 'signs of recovery', which argues with the play's 'struggling to remain operational' (crop or cover the strap). 'Retail giant Amazon's' at 81-84 is fine but skippable.

candidates.name: 04-sky-live-aws-system-underpins-millions
candidates.event: AWS us-east-1 outage, 20 October 2025; Sky News live coverage (93 minutes)
candidates.speaker: presenter at desk (presumed; captions only)
candidates.quote: And we now know that the cause of this is Amazon Web Services. This is Amazon's cloud computing service. And AWS provides cloud computing services on the internet. And what this means, in sort of layman's terms, is that companies can rent storage or databases instead of having to manage, build and run their own physical infrastructure or hardware. This AWS system underpins millions of large companies. And so, when you get an issue with it, you're going to see multiple companies having problems as we did today.

candidates.name: 04-bbc-aws-underpins-huge-proportion
candidates.event: AWS us-east-1 outage, 20 October 2025; BBC News channel with senior technology reporter Chris Vallance live from Glasgow
candidates.speaker: correspondent on a remote feed (small window), voice over a Downdetector logo wall
candidates.quote: What seems to be behind this, and this is what some of the affected organizations are saying, is a problem with Amazon Web Services. Now that's not a company that many people will have heard of, but its technology underpins just a huge proportion of the web services, the web apps that we use every day. Essentially companies use Amazon Web Services to provide computing power, to store their data, to process the information that they have on Amazon's computers, enabling them to operate their business. So when Amazon Web Services goes wrong, all the companies that depend on Amazon Web Services have problems.
candidates.onScreenText: BBC bug top left in the remote window; no chyron in the checked window
candidates.picture: Chris Vallance in a small picture-in-picture box top left (Glasgow skyline behind him, laptop in front), with a full-screen grid of Downdetector logos (Snapchat, Ring, Roblox, AWS, Lloyds Bank, Amazon, Halifax, Signal, Zoom, Canva, Fortnite, HMRC) scrolling behind
